Subject: Batch job finalization SLAs and retry/idempotency questions

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. A few follow-ups from our engineering and procurement teams around the async/batch guarantees:

- Our nightly enrichment pipeline submits batches of ~120k records and expects a finalization window of 6 hours. Can Redwood commit to a job completion SLA for that scale?
- If a job fails midway due to infra hiccups, what retry semantics do you recommend? We need an approach that avoids duplicate downstream writes.
- We're also curious what carveouts you expect for infra outages and what remediation (credits/SLO adjustments) looks like.

Do you have a proposed SLA paragraph we can share with procurement? I can loop in legal if needed, but wanted to get the technical scope aligned first.

Thanks,
Daniel

Head of Data Engineering — Acme Analytics

From: priyom_das@redwood.com

Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Batch job finalization SLAs and retry/idempotency questions

Hi Daniel — great questions.

Short answer: we can propose a pragmatic SLA and a safety-first retry/idempotency model that matches your nightly cadence. Attached is a draft SLA paragraph plus a short diagram of our recommended idempotency token flow. Key points:

1) Completion window: For batches up to 200k records, we propose a 99.5% completion window of 6 hours measured from job submission to finalization (finalization = all output blobs available + success manifest).

2) Retries and idempotency: We rely on client-supplied job_id + per-record idempotency tokens. Retries are safe so long as the same tokens are reused; our runtime deduplicates by token before finalizing outputs. We also offer an assisted mode where we generate server-side tokens and return a receipt. See retry-idempotency-diagram.png.

3) Carveouts: SLA excludes region-wide provider incidents, customer-side malformed payloads, and scheduled maintenance published with >=72h notice. For infrastructure incidents we propose pro-rated credit tiers (detailed in the attached PDF).

I copied Karthik and Dev to confirm feasibility and to flag any implementation constraints we should call out to Acme.

Next step: if this looks reasonable we'll produce a redlineable paragraph for your procurement/legal team.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0123

Attachments: acme_sla_draft_v2.pdf; retry-idempotency-diagram.png

Quick internal note — scope and numbers look good but two implementation items:

- For 200k records we need to guarantee KV cache sizing so we don't OOM during dedupe. Ops can reserve a temporary async pool for Acme's nightly window (configurable).
- For 'assisted-mode' token issuance, Dev says we can emit a server_receipt that is idempotent for 72 hours; beyond that we'd need a re-ingest. Suggest adding 'receipt TTL: 72h' to the SLA.

If you'd like, I can produce the technical blurb for the SOW.

— Kar
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions Architecture — Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:54:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Batch job finalization SLAs and retry/idempotency questions

Ack — operational constraints:

- We'll allocate a burst pool with 4x baseline capacity for the 6-hour window. That requires a reserved node slice attached to the customer's Dedicated pool during the nightly window; ops will automate the slice by cron.
- We'll support user-supplied idempotency tokens and server_receipt with 72h TTL. We'll also expose a 'finalization-manifest' endpoint so downstream systems can poll and avoid double-processing.

I'll add these bullets to the SLA draft. Dev
Dev Patel
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Batch job finalization SLAs and retry/idempotency questions

Hi Daniel — attaching an updated SLA paragraph and a short mutual action plan (MAP) that maps delivery milestones to contract language. Highlights:

- SLA: 99.5% of batches <=200k records will reach finalization within 6 hours. Measurement window is submission timestamp -> finalization manifest timestamp.
- Receipt TTL: server_receipt (when used) guarantees idempotent retry semantics for 72 hours. Customers can also supply per-record idempotency_token which is retained for 30 days for dedupe/forensics (storage cost apply).
- Operational carveouts: provider outages, customer malformed payloads, and force majeure. For infra incidents we will offer tiered service credit up to 10% of monthly committed fee for sustained breaches (>=2 consecutive hours impacting >=50% of Acme's nightly jobs).
- Remediation plan: auto-fallback to a lower-latency model variant for partial results, and an engineering callback playbook.

Please review the attached acme_sla_draft_v2.pdf and mutual-action-plan.xlsx. If procurement wants redlines we'll route to legal.

Best,
Priyom

Attachments: acme_sla_draft_v2.pdf; mutual-action-plan.xlsx
